title: Phase 2 Hadoop Modernization
opportunity: The Provider shall execute Phase 2 of the Client's Hadoop modernization roadmap. This engagement focuses on the systematic migration of identified active workloads from the legacy Hadoop ecosystem to Google Cloud Platform (GCP). The Provider will employ a modular, Move Group-based agile execution approach to ensure seamless transition and minimal business disruption. By leveraging this iterative methodology, the migration will prioritize risk mitigation and operational continuity. The Provider will work closely with the Client to ensure that all targeted workloads are successfully modernized, optimized, and validated within the Google Cloud environment, setting a robust foundation for future data scalability and analytics maturity.

Modernization Strategy: The solution centers on modernizing the Client's legacy Hadoop ecosystem by migrating its data platform to Google Cloud Platform (GCP). This transition uses an agile, sprint-based delivery model grouped into logical Move Groups. The implementation leverages the Provider's automation-led accelerators (Migration Birds) to ensure maximum speed, operational accuracy, and overall efficiency.

Onix Automation-Led Accelerators (Migrat: Eagle (The Planner): Utilized extensively during Phase 1 for deep workload discovery, comprehensive infrastructure assessment, structural dependency lineage tracking, and strategic move-group planning.
Raven (The Transformer): Systematically automates the conversion of complex legacy codebases, including Hive, Spark, Impala, and Oozie, to native GCP functional equivalents.
Pelican (The Validator): Ensures 100% data reconciliation and validation between the legacy Hadoop environment and the target GCP environment without necessitating risky or redundant data movement.
Condor (The Transporter): Facilitates the rapid, secure creation and deployment of robust automated data ingestion pipelines.

Target State Technology Mapping: Batch Ingestion: The Provider shall migrate batch ingestion workloads from Sqoop, Kafka, StreamSets, and Spark to Google Cloud Dataflow.
ETL/ELT Processing: Processing frameworks will be migrated from Apache Spark, Hive, Trino, and Impala to Serverless Dataproc and BigQuery.
SQL Query Engine: All query engines will be transitioned from Hive, Trino, and Impala strictly to BigQuery.
Orchestration: Workload orchestration will migrate from legacy Oozie environments to Cloud Composer (Airflow).
Data Storage (Lake & Warehouse): Storage systems will transition from HDFS, NetApp S3, and Hive Tables to Google Cloud Storage (GCS) and BigQuery.
Reporting & BI: The Client will retain the MicroStrategy platform; however, the Provider will repoint all necessary data connections directly to BigQuery.
Streaming: Existing streaming infrastructure will migrate from Kafka and Streamsets to Kafka and Google Cloud Dataflow.
Monitoring/Search: Observability services will migrate from ELK and Grafana to native ELK and Grafana implementations hosted on GCP.

Security & IAM: The Provider will implement standard GCP Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies, configure encryption protocols for data at rest and in transit, and establish rigid network security boundaries.

Data Load & Validation Workflow: Historical Load: The Provider shall extract historical data files from HDFS and deposit them into designated GCS buckets utilizing gsutil or distcp. Subsequently, data will be meticulously copied from GCS into BigQuery leveraging the GCP bqload utility, with the entire process seamlessly orchestrated via Cloud Composer.
Incremental & Parallel Processing: Legacy data pipelines, encompassing Day 0, Day 1, and Day 2 snapshots, will run in parallel alongside the newly converted GCP pipelines to verify integrity.

Validation: The Pelican validation accelerator will automatically compare source data residing in Hive against target data in BigQuery at a highly granular cell and row level to guarantee total functional parity before any production cutover is initiated.

Core Migration Activities: Source System Integration: The Provider shall establish and configure incremental data ingestion pipelines from existing source systems, including Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS), flat files, and Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), directly into the Google Cloud Platform.

Code Conversion & Refactoring: The Provider will systematically convert all in-scope database objects, such as tables and views, into highly optimized, BigQuery-compatible schemas and formats.

The Provider will convert legacy native scripts, including Sqoop imports, Scala, Spark SQL, Hive/Impala SQL scripts, and Trino queries, into fully managed GCP-native services such as Dataproc, Dataflow, and BigQuery.
The Provider will adapt and reutilize non-SQL Spark workloads utilizing Google Cloud Dataproc or functionally equivalent GCP processing frameworks.
The Provider will migrate and effectively reuse existing Python, Java, and Shell scripts within the new GCP environment wherever applicable and advantageous.

Core Migration Activities: Historical Data Migration: The Provider shall execute a comprehensive, one-time migration of historical data assets from the legacy Hadoop environment (HDFS and S3) into appropriate target GCP storage solutions (Cloud Storage and BigQuery).

Orchestration & Scheduling: The Provider shall implement robust task orchestration for all newly migrated workloads utilizing Cloud Composer (Airflow). The new scheduling logic will accurately reflect and mirror the existing Oozie schedules currently operating in the legacy environment.

End-to-end Pipeline Testing and Data Validation: The Provider will conduct rigorous testing protocols encompassing the unit testing of converted workloads, comprehensive historical data validation checks, and intensive parallel testing routines.

Report Repointing: The Provider shall repoint existing MicroStrategy reports from legacy Hadoop sources directly to BigQuery, specifically targeting the wireline access project or functionally similar reporting initiatives. Additionally, the Provider will deliver targeted enablement sessions to actively guide the Client through the repointing process, industry best practices, and common troubleshooting scenarios.
UAT Support: The Provider will deliver dedicated technical support during the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) phase to proactively assist the Client in validating the fully migrated workloads.

Warranty & Knowledge Transfer: The Provider shall supply a defined four-week warranty support period immediately following the final deployment. Concurrently, the Provider will conduct structured, comprehensive knowledge transfer sessions meticulously tailored for the Client's engineering and Business Intelligence (BI) teams.

Project Management Activities: Agile Ceremonies: The Provider shall continuously facilitate structured sprint planning sessions, host a comprehensive standard project kickoff meeting, and conduct weekly status alignment meetings.

Risk Management: The Provider will proactively identify, manage, and mitigate project risks, track ongoing complex issues, and actively monitor critical dependencies throughout the entire lifecycle of the migration engagement.

Optional Google Cloud Foundation Service: The Provider shall establish a foundational GCP Organization structure, defining core projects, distinct folder hierarchies, and applying baseline Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles and security policies.

The Provider shall provision the necessary BigQuery datasets and Google Cloud Storage buckets, ensuring the careful implementation of appropriate data lifecycle policies and stringent security configurations.

The Provider shall enable essential GCP services including Dataflow, Cloud Composer, and Cloud Build, while proactively configuring centralized logging frameworks, performance monitoring tools, and targeted billing alerts.
The Provider shall integrate Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP) services to systematically identify, classify, and prevent the unauthorized exposure of critical sensitive data assets.

Optional AI-Powered DataOps Managed Serv: The Provider shall deliver continuous 12-month, 24x7 operational coverage encompassing comprehensive Infrastructure Management, Data Pipeline Support, Data Quality Monitoring routines, holistic Data Observability, Cloud Cost Management, and secure Data Access Management.

System and Network Constraints: Overall external data transfer speeds and comprehensive pipeline execution timelines are strictly subject to the network bandwidth availability and stability between the Client's on-premises environment and the global Google Cloud infrastructure.

The projected total migration velocity and the overall project lifecycle timeline are entirely contingent upon the documented stability, continuous availability, and consistent performance of the legacy Hadoop environment and all interconnected upstream source systems.

Data Parity: The Provider shall establish and empirically verify 100% core data parity between the legacy Hadoop ecosystem and target BigQuery environments. This foundational parity will be meticulously confirmed via automated validation processes leveraging the Pelican accelerator for all identified historical data sets and all subsequent Day 1 and Day 2 incremental data loads.

MicroStrategy Integration: The Provider shall achieve successful integration, strict authentication, and continuous uninterrupted connectivity of the Client's MicroStrategy platform with the newly established GCP data infrastructure.

The Provider will establish and formally validate uncompromising data parity for all fundamental foundational base tables natively supporting the designated business-critical and relevant analytical reports.

Performance Parity and Improvement: The solution must consistently demonstrate objectively equivalent or measurably improved systemic performance metrics for all specifically designated business-critical dashboards.

The solution must guarantee that targeted data pipeline runtime execution is structurally superior to or entirely on par with the previously documented current Hive pipeline runtime execution metrics.

The final validation must confirm that generated report and user dashboard refresh times are fully on par with or demonstrably faster than the equivalent legacy reports previously operational on the Hive system.

Approval and Sign-off: All generated comprehensive Parallel Run validation reports must be thoroughly reviewed, formally accepted, and officially approved by the Client's explicitly designated Technical Subject Matter Experts (SMEs).
The Provider must achieve successful and formalized User Acceptance Testing (UAT) approval from all appropriately designated business user stakeholders representing the Client.

Knowledge Transfer: The Provider will successfully complete all designated complex technical enablement sessions and finalize the formal, documented handover of the Packaged Enablement Kit directly to the appropriately designated Client engineering and Business Intelligence (BI) teams.

Project and Migration Approach Assumptio: The core tactical migration strategy will operate strictly as a lift-and-shift migration approach, inherently assuming no substantial modifications to existing structural data models.

The Client's legacy Hadoop ecosystem and all deeply associated source system environments will maintain operational stability throughout the complete project duration; no major architectural or fundamental software changes will be introduced during this continuous period.

MicroStrategy repointing activities are strictly structurally confined to the designated wireline access project or a mutually agreed equivalent; all supplementary reporting or dashboard architectural requirements are explicitly formally excluded from the general project scope.

Any unforeseen underlying data quality issues, structural architectural errors, or systemic inconsistencies discovered within the legacy or source data environments may directly detrimentally impact and delay the projected timeline.

Any requested deviations concerning project activities, defined internal technology components, or established systemic volumetrics beyond the precisely documented scope will necessitate the immediate initiation of a formal project Change Request (CR) process.

The primary Google Cloud Organization and all critical target network infrastructure components will be fully pre-configured, rigorously tested, and securely functionally accessible prior to the official commencement of migration activities, unless the Optional Google Cloud Foundation Service Setup has been explicitly formally exercised and integrated into the overarching engagement.

Source baseline data volumes and processing complexity structural metrics will definitely not exceed the initial baseline measurements strictly established during the preliminary assessment phase by a calculated margin greater than 10%.

The Client shall highly facilitate completely timely and highly comprehensive structural knowledge transfer sessions deeply focusing on the current Hadoop architecture, complex foundational data models, existing systemic scheduling logic within Oozie, primary codebase nuances, and deeply associated business operational processes exactly as fundamentally required by the executing project team.
